prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Shape and peak position'. Three equal-size schematic plots arranged horizontally, headings 'Type A', 'Type B', 'Type C'. Each has identical axes: vertical 'Compliance', horizontal 'Pressure'; x-axis marked ONLY minus sign at left, 0 at midpoint, plus sign at right, and a faint vertical dotted guide through 0. Type A teal line: a single bell-shaped peak centred EXACTLY on the 0 guide, label underneath 'Near ambient'. Type B coral line: low flat horizontal line across plot with absolutely NO peak, label 'Flat'. Type C amber line: single bell-shaped peak CLEARLY LEFT of its 0 guide, label 'Negative pressure'. Same y-axis direction and same x-axis conventions all plots. Below middle plot note 'For B, check ear-canal volume'. Bottom 'Schematic patterns, not patient measurements'. No ear anatomy, diagnostic device branding or numeric cutoffs. Crisp graph geometry, warm hand-painted paper and curves.

clinicalSources.title: AAO-HNS: Clinical practice guideline—otitis media with effusion

teaching.question: How do type A, B and C tympanogram patterns differ?
teaching.answer: A peaks near ambient pressure, B is flat, and C peaks at negative pressure. A flat trace must be interpreted with ear-canal volume and the clinical findings.

title: Tympanogram shape and peak position
caption: Type A has a peak near ambient pressure, type B is flat, and type C peaks at negative pressure. A flat trace needs ear-canal-volume and clinical context; normal canal volume supports an effusion interpretation.
alt: Three schematic compliance-versus-pressure graphs show a central peak for A, a low flat line for B and a left-shifted peak for C.

review.notes: Three x axes consistently run negative→zero→positive. A peak is centred on zero, B line is flat, C peak is clearly left of zero while compliance remains upward. Ear-canal-volume qualifier present. No ear anatomy, cutoff values or patient measurement claim.
